proof.observed: --- PASS, all four subtests, ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/broker 7.318s. The fourth, added this round, is the tester's sequence: for three turns the old entry's exchange on a surviving old-configuration process takes the name back and the new entry's exchange on the new process takes it again, each take logged with both principals; while either holds it, that holder is answered 200 on every process, including the one whose configuration fixes the name for the other; the old process is then stopped, the holder does not move at the stop, and the new entry's next exchange leaves the name with the new entry while the old entry -- which no running configuration fixes it for now -- is refused 400 invalid_grant.

proof.criterion: No sentence of the body claims more than the code, and a reader finishes the paragraph knowing the binding is strong and the rollout window is untidy (the architect's standard, and its explicit request about the wording).
proof.surface: The body's session-name bullet, read against the two statements that implement it.
proof.command: the body, read against BindSession and ReserveSessions in internal/broker/oauthstore/exchange.go
proof.observed: The bullet reaches for no count at all: it says what moves a name (the retention running out; the caller a running broker's configuration fixes the name for taking it at its exchange) and says plainly that starting a replica moves nothing. It then states the two things a reader would otherwise discover: a re-point takes effect at the new entry's first exchange, so an entry that never exchanges leaves the name with its previous holder; and during a rollout the name alternates between the two generations' entries, with its bound named -- it lasts as long as any process of the old configuration still serves, so a stalled rollout prolongs it. It keeps the narrower true statement in place of the deleted clause (neither generation can leave the other's entry locked out), and says why the binding is not weakened: at every moment the name is held by an entry some running configuration fixes it for, and a principal no configuration designates is refused throughout.
proof.negativeControl: The phrases the tester and the reviewer caught are gone from the body: 'exactly two ways' and 'cannot take a name from each other' each return zero hits.
